scenes.headline: What is a black hole?
scenes.narration: Imagine a place where gravity is so strong that nothing can escape, not even light. That place is called a black hole.

scenes.headline: Born from giant stars
scenes.narration: Many black holes form when a very big star runs out of fuel and collapses in on itself.

scenes.headline: Gravity gets squeezed
scenes.narration: The collapse packs all of that star's stuff into a tiny space. The stronger the squeeze, the stronger the pull.

scenes.headline: The point of no return
scenes.narration: Around a black hole is an edge called the event horizon. Once something crosses it, there is no way back out.

scenes.headline: Seeing the invisible
scenes.narration: Black holes are dark, so scientists spot them by how they tug on nearby stars and gas. That gas glows as it swirls inward.

scenes.headline: Not a space vacuum
scenes.narration: A black hole only pulls things in when they get very close. A planet far away can orbit one safely, just like the Earth orbits the Sun.
scenes.body: Distance matters more than you might think.

scenes.headline: Keep asking questions
scenes.narration: The universe is full of mysteries, and black holes are some of the most amazing. Keep looking up and wondering why.
